title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers
tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

faults.what: The crop stays focused on the dark-shirted man rather than following the speakers; the light-shirted man's face is cut off at the left edge.
The woman is almost entirely outside the frame in every supplied output sample, so her answer is not presented with her face visible and centred.

judge.summary: The clip is portrait and caption-free, but its crop favours the central man instead of framing the questioner and then the woman.

must_haves.item: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
must_haves.why: The output frames are 9:16 portrait and show the same office scene and people.

must_haves.item: The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
must_haves.why: The light-shirted man is cut off along the left edge, while the crop favours the dark-shirted man.

must_haves.item: The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
must_haves.why: None of the supplied output frames shows her face; only small portions of her hair or shoulder appear at the right edge.

must_haves.item: Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
must_haves.why: The reported 10.1-second duration preserves approximately the requested length, but the transcript contains only the question. The original audio, both turns, and lip sync cannot be verified from the supplied evidence.

must_haves.item: The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.
must_haves.why: People and objects retain plausible proportions, and no captions are visible.
